summary: Meei-Hwa Chern is a scholar of philosophy, religious studies, and Buddhist studies who completed doctoral studies under John Raines (attested 2000). Chern has served as a visiting researcher at Academia Sinica.
Megan Bryson works in Buddhist studies, sinology, and religious studies. She studied at Stanford University and held a position at the University of Tennessee (attested 2017).
Megumu Honda (1931–2011) was a scholar of Indology and Buddhist studies who studied under Paul Tedesco and Rulon Wells. He served as a professor at Doho University (attested 1996).
Mei Ching Hsuan specializes in Tibetology. She earned a PhD at the University of Bonn (attested 2009), studying under doctoral supervisor Peter Schwieger and teacher Dieter Schuh.
Meiji Yamada (born 1937) is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Ryukoku University (attested 1962). He later served as a professor at Ryukoku University (attested 1963, 2007).

Meinrad Scheller (1921–1991) specialized in linguistics and Indology, studying at Paris and Zurich under Manu Leumann, Ernst Risch, and Julius Pokorny. He held professorships at Fribourg (1963), Munich (1968–1975), and Zurich (from 1975).
Meiping Li specializes in Buddhist studies. Li earned a Master of Arts degree at Fo Guang University under the supervision of Kirill Solonin (attested 2009).

Meir Shahar (born 1959) works in sinology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. After studying at Harvard University (~1987–1992), he became Associate Professor of Chinese Studies at Tel Aviv University (~1994).

Melissa R. Kerin specializes in history, archaeology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD at the University of Pennsylvania under Michael W. Meister and Deborah Klimburg-Salter, and held a professorship at Washington and Lee University (attested 2015).

Melvyn C. Goldstein (born 1938) works in Tibetology, linguistics, and history. He earned his BA at the University of Michigan (~1955–1959) and PhD at the University of Washington (~1960–1968), later serving as an anthropology professor at Case Western Reserve University (1968–2002).

Merab Mamardashvili (1930–1990) was a philosopher who studied at Moscow University (~1949–1954). He held posts at Moscow State University (~1968–1974), the Top Courses for Scriptwriters and Film Directors (~1977–1980), and Tbilisi State University (1987–1990).

Mervin Viggo Hanson specializes in Buddhist studies and sinology. He completed a PhD at the University of British Columbia (attested 1980) under doctoral supervisor Leon Hurvitz and also studied under Kathryn Ann Adelsperger Cissell.
Mettanando Bhikkhu is a scholar of Buddhist studies. He earned a PhD from the University of Hamburg under the supervision of Barend Jan Terwiel.

Michael Alram (born 1956) is a numismatist and historian who completed his doctorate and habilitation at the University of Vienna under Robert Göbl and Manfred Mayrhofer. He held key posts at the Kunsthistorisches Museum and the Austrian Academy of Sciences.

Michael Aris (1946–1999) was a Tibetologist and historian who studied at Durham and the University of London under David Snellgrove. He held appointments at Oxford, including St Antony's and Wolfson colleges, as well as Harvard University.
Michael Balk specializes in Indology and Tibetology. He completed doctoral studies at the University of Bonn by 1988 and held a post at the Prussian State Library (attested 1991).

Michael Baxandall (1933–2008) was an art historian educated at Cambridge, Pavia, and Munich. He held posts at the Victoria and Albert Museum, the Warburg Institute, the Courtauld Institute, the University of Oxford, UC Berkeley, and Cornell University.

Michael Bernays (1834–1897) studied at the University of Bonn and Heidelberg University, where he was taught by Adolf Holtzmann. He later held posts at Leipzig University (1872–1873) and the University of Munich (1873–1890).

Michael Carrithers (born 1945) works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and religious studies. He studied at Wesleyan and Oxford, then taught at Oxford and the London School of Economics before becoming Professor of Anthropology at Durham University.

Michael Comans specializes in Indology and philosophy. He studied under Swami Dayananda Saraswati, R. Krishnamurthi Sastri, and Jan Willem de Jong at the Australian National University, later serving as a faculty member at the University of Sydney (~1989–2002).
